section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1968
title: 4 The variations in the incidence of accidental deaths in the different regions result from a large number of factors peculiar to the regions such as topography of the area, population, level of industrialisation and other factors. Considering population as one of the major con-commitant variants, the volume of accidental deaths per one lakh of population was estimated for different States, Union Territories and Cities and is presented in Table 4. This tables shows that the maximum volume of accidental deaths was noticed in Maharashtra (43·5) followed by Madhya Pradesh (40·1) and West Bengal (30·3). The incidence of accidental deaths in all the Union Territories is only 2·5% of the all-India total. The volume of accidental deaths in the Cities under study is, on an average, significantly higher than the all-India volume viz. 39·5 as against 24·1. Among these, Bombay (59·7) recorded the highest volume of accidental deaths. TABLE 4
